_README: CALLS THAT ARE ON A CLIENT'S TRACKER BUT ARE NOT THAT CLIENT'S BUSINESS.
A closer who sells more than one offer books all of it into one tracker,
because the tracker belongs to the closer's calendar, not to the offer. So a
sale can be recorded correctly and still not be ours to count. Nothing in the
data says which offer a call was for — Brey's tracker has no Offer field, and
the closer, the price and the outcome all look identical either way.
WHY A LIST AND NOT A RULE. There is no signal that separates these safely.
The obvious candidate — money recorded as taken on the call that never
appears in the client's payment processor — was tested against Brey's live
account on 2026-08-22 and matched exactly two calls, one of which (Liam) was
an ordinary Funded Blueprint sale whose 'collected on call' figure had simply
been typed wrong. A rule like that would quietly delete a real sale every
time a payment failed to match. So exclusions are named by a person, one at a
time, with the reason attached.
THE COST OF THIS FILE, STATED PLAINLY: it only holds calls somebody thought
to add. As the other offer sells more, this list goes stale and the client's
revenue reads high, with nothing on any screen saying so. The durable fix is
an Offer field on the tracker that the closer sets. Until that exists, every
command that reads this file also prints how many calls it excluded, and the
Sales Command Center says on the page how many rows it left out, so the list
cannot rot silently.
MATCHED ON notion_page_id WHEN THE ENTRY CARRIES ONE, and otherwise on
call_date + prospect_name together. The page id is the tracker row's own
identifier and is exact; the name is a fallback for entries written before
the id was recorded. The fallback is not safe on its own: the 2026-08-22 row
below is named literally 'Unknown', and two Unknown rows on one date would be
indistinguishable, so excluding one would exclude both. Give every new entry
a notion_page_id.
BEFORE YOU ADD A ROW, ASK WHOP WHETHER THE MONEY ARRIVED. A tracker row with
no prospect email reads as unmatched whoever paid, so 'the processor never saw
this cash' is a statement about the missing email, not about whose sale it is.
One row was excluded on that reasoning on 2026-08-22 and put back on 2026-08-24
once the payment was found. Search the payments by the buyer's own name.
AN EXCLUDED CALL IS NEVER TURNED INTO A LEAD, so it cannot reach revenue, the
close rate or the funnel even if somebody later types an email onto the row.
TWO COPIES, ONE FILE. The Sales Command Center and the KPI dashboard deploy
independently and cannot read each other, so each repository carries its own
copy. Copy this file WHOLE; never edit one side. Both repos run
`npm run check:rules`, which compares the copies when they sit side by side.
